title: Food delivery model and ordering
idea: A food delivery model separates the live menu from the order: a cart serves one restaurant, and placing it freezes each item's price.
points: `Restaurant` owns its menu; `MenuItem` is an immutable record, replaced to change a price.
`Cart` is bound to one restaurant, so mixed kitchens are rejected at `add` time.
`OrderService.place` validates the cart, then copies each item into an `OrderLine` snapshot.
An `Order` never points at live menu objects, so menu edits cannot change receipts.

steps.caption: A `Restaurant` holds its menu as `MenuItem` records. A price change puts a new record under the same id.
The customer fills a `Cart`. The cart stores only item ids and quantities, not prices.
The cart is created for one restaurant. An item id from another menu is rejected immediately.
`OrderService` reads the cart and looks each id up again, catching items removed since they were added.
It creates an `Order` record. The order's list is copied with `List.copyOf`, so nobody can append to it.
Each `OrderLine` copies the name and unit price at this moment. The receipt is now history, not a view.

code.title: The problem: live menu objects
code.caption: The order holds references to shared, mutable menu items, so the receipt changes after checkout.

walk.text: Package-private, non-final fields: any class in the package can change a price, and every order sees it.
The order has no restaurant, so nothing stops two kitchens in one order.
Pizza and sushi land in one order. Which rider collects from which kitchen?
Quantity is modelled by adding the same object twice; there is no line or count.
A menu edit an hour later rewrites the customer's receipt. The bill no longer matches the payment.

code.title: The fix: cart, then snapshot
code.caption: A one-restaurant cart, a validating service, and an immutable order built from copied lines.

walk.text: `MenuItem` is a record with a compact constructor that rejects a missing id or a non-positive price.
The cart is tied to one restaurant at construction. It stores ids and counts only.
`add` rejects bad counts and foreign items; `merge` adds to an existing line.
`OrderLine` holds copied values. `List.copyOf` makes the order's lines unmodifiable.
Placing re-checks every item against the current menu, then freezes name and price.
The price rise after placing does not touch the order's total.

pitfalls: Storing `MenuItem` references in `Order` lets menu edits rewrite past receipts; copy the price.
Letting a cart hold several restaurants breaks pickup and rider assignment; bind it to one.
Skipping the menu re-check in `place` lets a removed or sold-out item reach the kitchen.

quiz.q: Same classes as the fix. What does this print?
quiz.why: `merge` sums both adds into one line of 3. The line copied 350 at placing, so the later 400 is ignored.

takeaway: The cart points at the live menu; the order holds a frozen copy.

starters: Should the cart be stored on the server or only in the app?
How would I model item add-ons like extra cheese or size options?
What should happen if the restaurant closes while a customer is checking out?
